text:
sara: heads-up — found a plaintext service account key inside a partner GCS backup blob: gs://partner-logs-us/backups/2026-03-20/dump.json. not public but contains credentials. tagging sec.
sec-bot: SecAlert: possible credential exposure detected by leak-scan. Created incident INC-1723 and attached blob hash. :warning:
mike: what's the SA email/id? any signs it was used recently?
sara: SA is redwood-partner-ingest@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com. file shows the json key blob and a timestamp 2026-03-20T02:11:05Z. sha256: 3b7f2e9c... (shortened)
jordan: I'll lead containment. suggested immediate steps: 1) delete the exposed key, 2) revoke any active tokens/keys, 3) create new SA key + deposit in Vault (kv-v2), 4) rewrap any customer secrets with new KMS version, 5) audit logs and RBAC tighten. Need oncall to delete key now.
natalie: I can delete the key now if you give the key id. share the key_id from the blob.
sara: key_id is 0123456789abcdef. here's the quick extraction i ran: `gsutil cat gs://partner-logs-us/backups/2026-03-20/dump.json | jq -r '.service_account_key.id'`
eli: recommend creating new KMS key version before rewrapping so we can rekey atomically: `gcloud kms keys versions create --key=wrapping-key --location=global --keyring=prod --key=wrapping-key` then use `gcloud kms keys versions add-iam-policy-binding` to limit to kms-wrappers group.
devops: also enable data-access audit logs for KMS and IAM on the partner project and enable Vault audit device if it's not already. quick IAM policy snippet to restrict wrap/unwarp:
```
principals:
  - group:kms-wrappers@redwood.com
bindings:
  - role:roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
    members: ["group:kms-wrappers@redwood.com"]
```
mike: good. jordan — can you open a PR for the Vault KV changes (restrict to path `secret/data/partners/ingest/*`, add write-only to service account?)
jordan: yup. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987 :eyes:
oncall-bot: Paging oncall-eng: incident INC-1723 has been created and requires immediate action. @oncall-eng
natalie: deleting exposed key now: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete 0123456789abcdef --iam-account=redwood-partner-ingest@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=partner-prod` — executing.
sara: after deletion, i'll scrub the backup copies from GCS and ask the partner to rotate any local copies. plan to run `gsutil rm gs://partner-logs-us/backups/2026-03-20/dump.json` once we snapshot evidence.
natalie: key deleted — command returned 200 OK.
mike: revoke any cached tokens too: `gcloud auth revoke --all` isn't sufficient; we should rotate any long-lived tokens and create new keys that are stored into Vault with a short TTL. eli to coordinate Vault ingestion procedure.
eli: i'll push a script that wraps the new key via KMS and stores to Vault with metadata and a 7-day rotation schedule. example: `vault kv put secret/partners/ingest key=@new_sa.json rotation=7d wrapping_kms=projects/.../keys/wrapping-key` (will add proper CLI in PR)
jordan: scheduling a 15m incident sync at 14:00 to coordinate partner outreach, infra, and platform. i'll add postmortem template and include prompt-based regression tests.
sara: taking a snapshot of the blob (local copy encrypted) and then removing the GCS object. also verifying access logs for reads between 02:00–04:00 UTC.
devops: after containment, follow-up items: 1) RBAC audit to ensure no broad `roles/owner` or wildcard members, 2) enable TTLs on SA keys where possible, 3) add leak-scan rule to flag backup buckets containing `service_account_key` fields.
mike: assign follow-ups in INC-1723 and tag owners. thanks everyone — update thread after the 14:00 sync.
